Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private connectivity follow-up & checklist

Hi Elliot / Angela —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on during the call so we can get the network preflight scheduled with our engineers: 

1) Desired deployment mode: Private VPC (Redwood Private control plane + PrivateLink peering). You mentioned keeping inference traffic in your VPC and using PrivateLink for control-plane signals.
2) Action items for FinOps: send network diagrams, CIDR ranges, NAT/egress architecture, security contact, and any proxy/mTLS requirements.
3) Redwood asks: confirm whether you prefer AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering (we recommended PrivateLink for least blast radius), whether you need egress IP allowlisting for model downloads, and if you plan to terminate TLS at a proxy.

Attached is our lightweight checklist to help collect everything (redwood_vpc_requirements_checklist.xlsx). Please add the network doc you referenced if convenient. 

Proposed next steps:
- FinOps to share network diagram + point of contact (by EOD Friday).
- We’ll schedule a 1-hr preflight call (network + security) with Karthik and Vanessa on our side.
- Karthik will confirm specific ports and FQDNs needed for PrivateLink and telemetry.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update the plan.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Grace —

Appreciate the recap and the checklist. Quick answers up front:
- We are leaning toward PrivateLink for control-plane + NAT egress for model artifacts.
- Our security team prefers allowlisting on egress IPs rather than opening broad CIDR ranges.
- We will need to ensure traffic to telemetry endpoints can be routed via our proxy (we use an outbound TLS intercepting proxy).

I’m attaching our internal network diagram and a brief note from our security team that outlines current proxy behavior. Our security lead Angela Ruiz (cc’d) will be the primary point for the preflight.

We also have a couple of follow-ups: what SLA tiers are available for Private VPC customers, and whether Dedicated GPU pools are required for predictable throughput (we have bursty batch jobs).

Thanks,
Elliot Harper
VP Engineering — FinOps Co
elliot.harper@finops.co

Subject: Re: Private connectivity follow-up & checklist — technical clarifications

Hi Elliot / Angela —

Thanks for the diagram, that’s helpful. A few technical clarifications from our infra team before the preflight so the call is efficient: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering: PrivateLink is preferred for control-plane traffic (smaller firewall footprint and no long-lived route changes). If you choose PrivateLink we’ll need an endpoint service in your account and your network team needs to accept the endpoint (we can provide CloudFormation to simplify).

2) IP allowlist & egress: for model artifact fetches we can either provide static egress IPs (for a paid dedicated egress pool) or support dynamic egress through your NAT. If you need static outbound IPs for allowlisting, call that out and we’ll scope Dedicated capacity + egress allocation in the quote.

3) Ports/FQDNs: control-plane uses TCP 443 (TLS) to a small set of FQDNs. Telemetry and metrics endpoints are also TLS; if your TLS-inspecting proxy performs MITM, we’ll need to exchange CA certs for certificate pinning avoidance or use mutual TLS — which is doable but needs security sign-off.

4) Subnet recommendations: create a dedicated pair of private subnets for the PrivateLink interface endpoints / target ENIs and a route to the NAT gateway for model downloads (if you prefer NAT). We can share a short CloudFormation template for recommended subnets and security groups.

I’m attaching a short snippet that our security team typically shares as a starting point for enterprise customers (example_security_policy_snippet.txt).

If you confirm whether you want static egress IPs or NAT-for-artifacts, we’ll prepare a short quote and a preflight agenda. I’m available Friday afternoon or early next week for the network deep-dive.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

- Preflight call: propose Wednesday 2027-06-23 at 10:00am PT — agenda will be: 1) topology review, 2) ports/FQDNs, 3) cert/pinning & proxy behavior, 4) timing for egress decision and pricing impact.

I’ll put a tentative calendar invite on both sides and include the HubSpot deal link (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345). If that time doesn’t work, reply with alternatives and we’ll adjust.

Grace
